record.original_question: Determine whether D_mu^s(M) admits a closed L2 geodesic when M is a compact surface of genus at least two or a bounded planar domain with at least two holes.

evidence.quote: Problem 10. Does there exist a closed geodesic in Dµs (M )? Note that the Kelvin–Helmholtz theorem implies that any geodesic loop in Dµs (M ) is necessarily a closed geodesic. One may try to construct a suitable Lyapunov function (see below) to show that in this case a geodesic never returns to its initial configuration. Yet another basic problem concerns the fluid configuration space Dµ (M ) itself. As an infinite dimensional (Frechet) Lie group it can be viewed as a Riemannian homogeneous space equipped with a right-invariant L2 metric (1.3). However, the group Dµ (M ) is not a Riemannian symmetric space. This means that the (geodesic) central symmetry about the identity in Dµ (M ) is not an isometry of the L2 -metric. In this respect, we have to keep in mind that the geodesic symmetry is not the same as the group-theoretic symmetry, i.e. the map g → g −1 . The latter (group- theoretical) inversion maps a right-invariant metric on the group into a left-invariant one, hence, indeed, it is not an isometry. artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be either a closed (compact, boundaryless) smooth surface of genus $g\ge 2$, or a smooth bounded planar domain with at least two holes (i.e. whose boundary has at least three connected components), equipped with a smooth area form $\mu$. For an integer $s>\dim(M)/2+1$, let $\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ denote the group of orientation- and volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of $M$ of Sobolev class $H^s$ (in the planar case, additionally fixing the boundary). It is a smooth infinite-dimensional Hilbert manifold and a topological group, and it carries the right-invariant weak Riemannian metric induced at the identity by the $L^2$ inner product
$$\langle u,v\rangle_{L^2} \;=\; \int_M \langle u(x),v(x)\rangle\, d\mu(x)$$
on divergence-free tangent vector fields. A geodesic of this metric corresponds to a solution of the incompressible Euler equation on $M$.

Question. Does there exist a non-constant closed geodesic of this $L^2$ metric in $\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$, i.e. a smooth curve $\eta:\mathbb{R}\to \mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ which is a geodesic and satisfies $\eta(t+T)=\eta(t)$ for some $T>0$ and all $t$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of existence of a closed $L^2$ geodesic in the volume-preserving diffeomorphism group on higher-genus surfaces or multiply-connected planar domains appears to remain open. Recent work by Drivas and Torres de Lizaur (generalizing earlier results of Ebin) shows that geodesics on such groups cannot have transverse self-intersections—any returning geodesic must be periodic—but this only rules out non-periodic recurrence and does not produce or exclude closed geodesics. No source found that constructs such a closed geodesic or proves its non-existence in the stated setting.

status_evidence.title: Geodesics on group of measure preserving diffeomorphisms do not self-intersect
status_evidence.snippet: Drivas and Torres de Lizaur generalize Ebin's result that geodesics in the group of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms cannot transversely self-intersect, to surfaces of any genus and planar domains with any number of boundary components.
status_evidence.claim: The non-self-intersection result reduces the closed-geodesic problem to ruling out recurrence but does not resolve existence of closed L^2 geodesics.

status_evidence.title: Singular sets of Riemannian exponential maps in hydrodynamics
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on the exponential map and conjugate points in the L^2 geometry of the volume-preserving diffeomorphism group, listing the existence of closed geodesics in higher-genus and multiply-connected cases among open questions.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of closed L^2 geodesics on D^s_mu(M) in these cases is still treated as an open problem in current literature.
